newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slips on subdued Nokia, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slips on subdued Nokia, profit-taking.

text.p: Shares fell in fair trade on Tuesday with Nokia subdued and with profit-taking biting into gains of financial sector shares, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 0.4 percent to 2398.84, with decliners leading advancing issues 48 to 38. Volume was moderate at 342 million markka.
"After the strong rise in New York yesterday, it's no wonder we recoiled a bit today," one broker said.
Nokia fell 2.60 markka to 262.40, failing to match its lower New York opening.
Brokers said investors were taking profits in insurers Pohjola and Sampo after recent gains sparked by talk of a major reshuffle in the Nordic finance sector.
But banking share Merita bucked the trend.
Merita A put on 0.10 markka to close at 14.80. Brokers said foreign investors continued to show interest in the bank share and that it was also helped by lower bond yields.
Pohjola fell 1.50 to 103.00 markka, while Sampo closed flat at 339.00 off its intrasession high of 342.00 markka.
State-controlled chemicals group Kemira rose 1.90 markka to 55.50 in fairly brisk trade, but in the absence of company news brokers could only guess at the reason for the rise.
"There has been a lot of overseas demand for Kemira," one broker said. "It could be a post-share issue phenomena."
The government recently sold 18 million Kemira shares.
UPM-Kymmene gained 0.40 markka to 90.00, but the forestry sub-index was a shade lower as Enso fell 0.30 to 35.20 and Metsa-Serla softened 0.50 to 30.00 markka.
"The upturn in the forestry sector simply isn't here yet," one broker said.
The Thanksgiving holiday the U.S. on Thursday was seen dampening trade in Helsinki in the latter half of the week.
